doc.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996

title: Clark Terry's playing and why Rosengarden takes the gigs
summary: He praises Clark Terry's playing and explains he takes jobs for love of playing and the company.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Looking back: no regrets, what it all meant

blocks.x: Didn’t he play good last night?
Oh, man. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -14-
I can’t remember him playing this well for a long time. I thought there was a period there where boy are we going to miss him.
Well he put in a year last year, from the looks of his schedule doing his 75th birthday tour, that would have taxed anybody.

Well you want to know something? If he hadn’t done it, he would have melted. My wife gets mad at me sometimes because I take jobs. And I know she realizes I do it because I want to play, I love to play. I can’t believe people pay me large sums of money for doing simply what I love to do. And the first question I ask is who am I fighting? Who am I playing with? And when I got called to do this, you know Milt Fillius called me and he told me, “I’d like you to do this thing at the school, up at the college,” and I’d say, “Great Milt,” because we’re friends, and, “Who am I fighting?” you know, whose going to be there? He says well Clark, you know, and Johnny Bunch and Bob Haggart, Kenny Davern and Dan Barrett. Wow.
That’s right. Beats the hell out of working.
